desc:
Encoding. A singly linked structure with n nodes is given as a successor array. The nodes are numbered 0..n-1 and succ[i] is the number of the node that follows node i, or -1 if node i has no next node. The list starts at node 0 (its head).

Follow succ from the head. If the walk reaches -1 the list has no cycle and the answer is 0. Otherwise the walk eventually runs around a loop of nodes that repeats forever; return the number of nodes in that loop.

Only nodes reachable from node 0 count; loops among unreachable nodes must be ignored. For succ = [1,2,3,4,2] the walk is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 2, ..., the loop is 2, 3, 4 and the answer is 3.
constraints: Some nodes may be unreachable from node 0; they are ignored
hints: A map from node to the step number at which you first stood on it gives the length directly when you step on a node twice. It needs O(n) memory.
First detect the cycle with a slow and a fast pointer. When they meet, the meeting node is inside the cycle.
Keep one pointer at the meeting node and walk another from succ[meeting] until it returns to that node, counting the steps. The count is the cycle length.
editorial: Run Floyd's algorithm: slow moves one node, fast two. If fast falls off the list there is no cycle, answer 0. If they meet, the meeting node lies on the cycle (a pointer can only meet the other one inside the loop).

Starting from that meeting node, follow succ until you come back to it, counting steps. You go around the loop exactly once, so the count is its length. The detection phase is O(n) and the counting phase is at most the cycle length, so the whole algorithm is O(n) time and O(1) space.
The step-number map is the alternative: when a node is reached for the second time at step j and was first reached at step i, the cycle length is j - i.
